slides.title: Transformations
slides.notes: Open the lecture by telling students that transformations are not decorative symmetries added after geometry is built. In this chapter they are tests for the connection itself. A map, a vector field, or a local germ earns geometric meaning by preserving parallel transport, curvature data, metric data, or analytic normal-coordinate information.

slides.title: Route Through Chapter VI
slides.notes: Use this route slide to prevent the chapter from becoming a list of named propositions. The spine is preservation. First a map preserves the connection, then a vector field preserves it infinitesimally, then the Riemannian case adds the metric, and the final sections ask how much initial data determines the symmetry.

slides.title: Affine Maps Preserve Parallelism
slides.notes: Frame affine mappings as maps that respect the connection before they respect any metric. A good classroom move is to draw one curve and one transported vector, then apply the map. If the transported image agrees with transport in the target connection, the map is passing the chapter's main preservation test.

slides.title: The Frame-Bundle Test
slides.notes: This slide connects Chapter VI back to the principal-bundle language established earlier. The point is not to make students memorize two forms. The point is that the solder form and connection form together encode the entire affine structure, so preserving both is a compact and testable version of preserving the connection.

slides.title: The Affine Transformation Group
slides.notes: Stress that the Lie group statement is a structural payoff. It means the symmetries are not an arbitrary collection of maps. Once the connection is fixed, the accepted transformations have enough rigidity that one-parameter subgroups and their vector-field generators become the right language for the rest of the chapter.

slides.title: Infinitesimal Affine Transformations
slides.notes: Introduce infinitesimal affine transformations as the derivative version of the preceding group. Students should see that the vector field is being judged by its flow. If the flow keeps the connection stable to first order, then the lifted field upstairs commutes with the standard horizontal directions that encode parallel displacement.

slides.title: Four Faces Of The Same Condition
slides.notes: Treat the equivalence as a translation table. The same condition can be read geometrically from flows, upstairs from the frame bundle, algebraically from an operator identity, or diagnostically from induced behavior on torsion and curvature. This is a good moment to ask students which formulation they would use for a computation.

slides.title: Completeness Turns Local Flow Into Global Flow
slides.notes: The proof idea is worth making visual. Completeness is not a decorative hypothesis; it prevents the flow from running out of manifold before the affine condition can be propagated. The frame-bundle argument uses horizontal accessibility and vertical changes of frame to extend the local generator to a full one-parameter transformation group.

slides.title: Isometries Are Orthogonal Affine Maps
slides.notes: Now specialize from connections to Riemannian geometry. The orthonormal frame bundle gives a clean picture: an isometry cannot just move frames; it must move orthonormal frames to orthonormal frames. The Levi-Civita connection turns this metric preservation into affine preservation, so the earlier machinery becomes available.

slides.title: Killing Fields And The Skew Test
slides.notes: Present Killing fields as infinitesimal isometries, not as mysterious vector fields with a name attached. The skew condition is the key computational test: a skew endomorphism rotates or shears within the metric conventions without changing inner products to first order. This prepares the holonomy and Ricci restrictions that follow.

slides.title: Holonomy Reads The Infinitesimal Part
slides.notes: This slide is about where the infinitesimal data can live. The tensor A sub X compares two ways of moving: by the flow of X and by the connection. Holonomy records what parallel transport can produce, so the chapter uses normalizer and compactness arguments to restrict the allowable mismatch.

slides.title: Ricci Tensor As A Trace Constraint
slides.notes: Define Ricci carefully but visually. The chapter needs Ricci because a trace of curvature can be integrated or sign-tested more directly than the full curvature tensor. In lecture, emphasize that Ricci summarizes how the curvature operator responds across all directions, which makes it effective for controlling infinitesimal symmetries.

slides.title: Negative Ricci Removes Continuous Isometries
slides.notes: Do not present this as a magic theorem about negativity. Explain the mechanism: Killing fields preserve the metric, so analytic identities convert their derivative data and the Ricci trace into a nonnegative quantity that cannot coexist with strict negative Ricci unless the field is zero. Then connect the infinitesimal result to finiteness of isometry groups on compact manifolds.

slides.title: Extending Local Affine Isomorphisms
slides.notes: The extension section is a local-to-global machine. The key idea is that analytic maps which agree in enough initial data cannot fork silently. Along a chain of neighborhoods, the local affine isomorphism continues, and simple connectivity prevents different chains from creating incompatible answers after going around a loop.

slides.title: The Equivalence Problem In Normal Coordinates
slides.notes: The equivalence problem asks for a practical recognition rule. Normal coordinates turn a connection into a controlled collection of coefficients near a base point. The chapter shows that torsion, curvature, and their derivative data can be organized so that matching the right jets produces a local affine equivalence.

slides.title: Parallel Torsion And Curvature Produce Models
slides.notes: This slide gathers the final equivalence results into one picture. Parallel torsion and curvature mean the invariants do not drift under parallel displacement, so normal-coordinate expansions become stable. With completeness and simple connectivity, the local affine equivalence can be pushed to a global model identification.

slides.title: Lab Surface: Perturb One Hypothesis
slides.notes: Use the lab slide to connect the lecture back to the notebook's perturbation mindset. Students should practice changing one assumption at a time and predicting which invariant breaks. The aim is not to solve exercises from the source, but to make the hypotheses feel like active controls in a geometric experiment.

slides.title: Teaching Recap
slides.notes: Close by returning to the preservation hierarchy. A general diffeomorphism is too loose for this chapter. Affine transformations preserve the connection, isometries preserve the metric and hence the Levi-Civita connection, and infinitesimal versions expose the same ideas through vector fields. The final lesson is that local data can become global symmetry only under explicit rigidity hypotheses.
